anita: quick signal from the replay harness — seeing a ~18% p95 regression vs synthetic for the same q8 model and target batch size.
philip: ugh. is this the KV-cache aware run or the cold-cache baseline?
anita: warmed KV cache. replay used production traffic with session affinity. synthetic is our default constant prompt length generator.
liam: any diffs in client settings? keepalive / connection pooling?
anita: yes — replay clients were using short-lived connections (no keepalive) because the recorder replays had per-request sockets. synthetic harness uses persistent HTTP keepalive and pooled channels.
maria: that alone explains a lot — TLS+TCP handshake costs add up, and gRPC has its own channel warmup. did you try forcing `Connection: keep-alive` in the replay driver?
anita: tried a quick patch, got p95 back down ~7% but still ~10% off synthetic.
philip: could also be Nagle (small writes) or TLS record sizing. replay replays many tiny prompt fragments which could aggregate into multiple small TCP writes. set `TCP_NODELAY` in the client to disable Nagle?
liam: also check kernel-scheduler differences — synthetic harness runs on our bench boxes with tuned kernel for batching (tcp_tw_reuse, net.core.somaxconn). replay was run from CI workers.
perf-bot: PERF ALERT: job/replay-run-1959 — p95 increased 18% vs baseline. see https://perf.redwood/internal/1959
anita: attaching short trace snippet from our flame (trimmed):
```
server: dispatch_loop -> select_kernel(depth=32) -> quantized_eval -> kv_cache_lookup (hit=0.92)
client: tls_handshake (avg 14ms) -> tcp_connect (avg 11ms) -> write_chunks (avg 2.3ms, 3 chunks)
queue: batching_delay median 1.6ms, p95 8.9ms
```
philip: kernel selection note: when sequence length distribution varies, runtime picks different matmul kernels. replay traffic has more short/long-tail mixes so more small-seq kernels which have worse amortized overhead. Might need an override or hybrid kernel.
maria: worth testing with `--force-kernel=hybrid` and `--batch-max-wait-ms=1` on server side to see if batching heuristics recover.
liam: also reproduce locally but run replay driver with `--reuse-connections` and `--tcp-nodelay` flags. small script: 
```
# repro command (linux)
./replay-driver --record ./session.json --rate 200 --reuse-connections --tcp-nodelay --grpc-keepalive=300s
ab -n 10000 -c 50 -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  -p payload.json http://bench-host/generate
```
anita: did the `--reuse-connections` + `--tcp-nodelay` run — p95 now within 2% of synthetic. TLS handshake still contributes ~10ms for new connections though.
philip: conclusion: bench mismatch is mostly client-side. For apples-to-apples we must ensure replay harness reuses connections and mirrors keepalive, TCP_NODELAY, and gRPC channel args. note this in the docs and add default flags to replay tool.
maria: also create a short test to toggle kernel selection to see if any residual gap is runtime-internal. file a perf ticket if hybrid kernel gives different tails.
liam: I'll open infra PR to pin kernel tunables on CI bench runners so synthetic and replay use the same network stack settings.
anita: created issue: PERF-2345 describing repro steps, flags, and initial traces. assigning to phillip for kernel follow-up. :thumbsup:
sre-bot: deploy accepted: bench-runner image updated with tcp_nodelay defaults.
philip: thanks — next steps: (1) replay tool defaults, (2) CI bench runner kernel parity, (3) try `--force-kernel=hybrid` and collect new traces, (4) consider adding client-side connection reuse checks into perf gating.
anita: will post a short follow-up with the exact AB numbers and the minimal repro later today.
